title: Multi-Flow streaming performance is pretty bad (maybe related to large tool call messages)
body:
### Bug Description

I have a multi-flow setup where an Agent is calling another flow (that has another agent) the called flow/agent is painfully slow. I can bring it up in the playground and it's streaming abnormally slow and I have noticed that there's a single python thread running at 100%. It seems like there's some sort of spin loop happening slowing everything down. 

I'm not really able to figure out how to profile this. 

A few more details:
Flow A is primary flow with basic Chat Input, Agent and Chat Output and has Flow B connected as a tool
Flow B has the same Chat Input, Agent and Chat Output with a Python based tool connected that does return a fair bit of data. 

I thought I had seen in the process of looking at the API that while streaming it keeps streaming the same message over and over with additional data. If this includes the tool call message that message will be bigger and bigger and bigger and then when the agent starts adding to it, it's going to be humongous. 

### Reproduction

Create Flow "Tool" with Chat Input, Agent, Chat Output, connect a tool to Agent that returns a lot of data and agent instructions to parse the data
Create Flow "Test" with Chat Input, Agent, Chat Output, connect Flow "Tool" as a Tool to that agent.
Ask Flow Test about something related to tool data

### Expected behavior

It will work and be usable... 

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Operating System

Linux

### Langflow Version

1.5.0.post2 in Docker

### Python Version

None

### Screenshot

_No response_

### Flow File

_No response_

                 if msg.flow_id and isinstance(msg.flow_id, str):
                     msg.flow_id = UUID(msg.flow_id)
                 session.add(msg)
-                await session.commit()
-                await session.refresh(msg)
                 updated_messages.append(msg)
             else:
                 error_message = f"Message with id {message.id} not found"
                 await logger.awarning(error_message)
                 raise ValueError(error_message)
+
+        # Batch commit all updates at once
+        await session.commit()
+
+        # Skip refresh during commit - the msg objects already have the updated values
+        # Refresh is only needed if we need database-generated values (like timestamps)
+        # For streaming performance, we skip this extra round-trip
+
         return [MessageRead.model_validate(message, from_attributes=True) for message in updated_messages]

+        """Send a message with optional database update control.
+
+        Args:
+            message: The message to send
+            id_: Optional message ID
+            skip_db_update: If True, only update in-memory and send event, skip DB write.
+                           Useful during streaming to avoid excessive DB round-trips.
+                           Note: This assumes the message already exists in the database with message.id set.

+        # If skip_db_update is True and message already has an ID, skip the DB write
+        # This path is used during agent streaming to avoid excessive DB round-trips

+            # Create a fresh Message instance for consistency with normal flow
+            stored_message = await Message.create(**message.model_dump())
+            self._stored_message_id = stored_message.id
+            # Still send the event to update the client in real-time
+            # Note: If this fails, we don't need DB cleanup since we didn't write to DB
+            await self._send_message_event(stored_message, id_=id_)
+        else:
+            # Normal flow: store/update in database
+            stored_message = await self._store_message(message)
 
-        self._stored_message_id = stored_message.id

-            complete_message = ""

-                stored_message.text = complete_message
-                stored_message = await self._update_stored_message(stored_message)
-            else:
-                # Only send message event for non-streaming messages
-                await self._send_message_event(stored_message, id_=id_)
-        except Exception:
-            # remove the message from the database
-            await delete_message(stored_message.id)
-            raise
+            self._stored_message_id = stored_message.id
+            try:
+                complete_message = ""

+                    self._should_stream_message(stored_message, message)
+                    and message is not None

+                ):
+                    complete_message = await self._stream_message(message.text, stored_message)
+                    stored_message.text = complete_message
+                    stored_message = await self._update_stored_message(stored_message)
+                else:

+                raise
         self.status = stored_message
